cohort: 3274 mother-child pairs recruited from New York State (excluding New York City) between 2008 and 2010, as part of the Upstate KIDS Study
finding: Neonates born via planned cesarean delivery had significantly lower levels of IgA, IgG(3), and IgG(4) compared to those born vaginally.
mod_finding: Planned cesarean delivery was associated with lower levels of IgA, IgG(3), and IgG(4) in neonates.
